provenance: Telephone call, 2026-09-03, Larry's son asking the tier-1 questions from the interview guide and typing Larry's answers as he spoke them. The Camp Zama date question had been promoted to the head of the guide that morning. Raw capture: research/interviews/breakfast-questions.md, annotated in place under each question.
text: About in the middle of the tour. The US Embassy is what was blown up or their offices. Pretty sure it was the Embassy. I heard it was the Vietcong who did it. I was about a block away, I think I was at the Papillon and it rocked the building when it went off.
researchNotes: This dates an event the archive had been unable to place. The US Embassy in Saigon was bombed by the Viet Cong on 30 March 1965 - a car bomb on Ham Nghi Boulevard that killed about 22 and wounded some 180. That is squarely in the middle of his tour, as he says. He places himself about a block away, at the bar he calls the Papillon, and says the blast rocked the building. Note the spelling: he renders it "Papillon" here, correctly French for butterfly, against "Papallon" in the VN-0120 comment of 2026-09-02. Held with one caution: on 2026-09-02 he described the building in VN-0120 as the Palace with a bar to its right, and the Embassy stood on Ham Nghi Boulevard rather than beside the Palace. Both accounts are his and neither is corrected.
